codex.text: The fixed adverse threshold is a high-risk overfit unless its selection is pre-registered and tested across multiple untouched time regimes, instruments, and cost-stress scenarios. The proposal never defines the loss metric, holding horizon, execution assumptions, or confidence bounds, so “above zero” expectancy and PF > 1.0 may be noise rather than a durable edge. A 2,611-exit aggregate does not establish that early exits improve outcomes versus the current SL/manual policy without paired counterfactual replay and drawdown/tail-risk validation.

opencode.text: The 90th-percentile threshold, rolling window, ATR timing, and suppression rules are underspecified, creating substantial degrees of freedom for overfitting. Repeatedly evaluating or tuning on the sealed holdout would contaminate it; acceptance also lacks minimum sample size, confidence intervals, and multiple-testing correction, so a 0.05R improvement and unchanged drawdown may be noise. The proposal does not require ExperimentRegistry recording or explicitly prohibit live deployment/config changes, and the arbitrary 70% trade-count floor is not justified by statistical power or risk objectives.

decision.rationale: REAL: falsifiable candidate registered as challenger council_the-aegis-mt5-demo-bot-is-running-the-in_e054ef for the validation pipeline

proposals.text: Test a volatility-regime filter that suppresses intelligent-firehose signals when 1-hour ATR is above its rolling 90th percentile. Evaluate it on the sealed holdout against the current validated-state baseline with identical spread and slippage assumptions. Accept only if net expectancy improves by at least 0.05R per trade, maximum drawdown does not increase, and trade count remains at least 70% of baseline.

Research a cost-aware loss-tail exit policy that exits trades at a fixed adverse-movement threshold before the current manual/SL tail losses, while preserving existing take-profit logic. The candidate passes only if a sealed, time-ordered holdout improves net expectancy from the measured −0.0143 to above zero and profit factor above 1.0, without reducing the validated-state gate or altering the champion. This is falsifiable because the current 2,611-exit sample shows a 0.76 profit factor and average losses nearly three times average wins.

question: The AEGIS MT5 DEMO bot is running the intelligent firehose with the validated-state gate. Given the current measured evidence, identify ONE concrete, falsifiable improvement candidate for the next research cycle. Do not modify code or the champion. Cite book corpus passages if relevant.

codex.text: Research a pre-registered, cost-aware loss-tail exit policy with the adverse threshold fixed before evaluation, preserving existing take-profit logic and validated-state gating. Evaluate it through paired counterfactual replay against the current SL/manual policy across multiple untouched time regimes and instruments, using the runner’s spread/slippage assumptions, a defined holding horizon, net per-trade expectancy, profit factor, maximum drawdown, and tail-loss quantiles. The candidate passes only if out-of-sample net expectancy exceeds zero and profit factor exceeds 1.0 with confidence bounds excluding the current-policy baseline, while showing no unacceptable drawdown or tail-risk deterioration under cost-stress scenarios. The result remains falsifiable because the existing 2,611-exit sample provides the baseline (PF 0.76; average losses nearly three times average wins), but no challenger may alter or replace the champion absent all promotion gates.

opencode.text: Pre-register ATR definition, completed-bar timing, rolling window, and a single threshold using development data only; freeze all suppression rules before one sealed-holdout evaluation. Record the experiment in `ExperimentRegistry`, use identical net-cost assumptions, and prohibit live config or deployment changes. Accept only with a pre-specified minimum holdout sample, bootstrap confidence intervals showing net expectancy improvement of at least 0.05R, non-increasing drawdown, and multiplicity-adjusted significance; set the trade-count requirement from pre-specified power and risk criteria rather than an arbitrary percentage.
